item.title: Boosie Badazz Runs Out Of Gas And Gets A Hand From King Harris
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Boosie Badazz says he figured he could get home without stopping for gas, then shows King Harris coming to help him.
item.content:encoded:
Boosie Badazz thought he’d make it home without stopping for gas. He wound up filming from the side of the road instead, and King Harris came to help him.

The clip circulated online on November 23. Boosie had been at a Hawks game the night before and figured he could make it home before his tank emptied.

“I knew I needed gas but I said I was just gonna make it home,” Boosie said in the clip, as quoted by AtlantaFi. He said he meant to stop but forgot.

Harris showed up dressed in a light suit with a scarf and hat. Boosie took a moment to compliment the outfit while the two joked about the situation.

This wasn’t the only time Boosie had been stuck recently. In another clip that circulated the previous week, he and his son Tootie Raww were left on a highway after running out of fuel. Boosie blamed Tootie in that one and stuck out his thumb while traffic passed, according to the report.

King, the son of T.I. and Tiny, had heard a different tone from Boosie when he and Tootie were shooting a music video. In footage that AllHipHop covered in September 2024, the two fathers wanted to know why their sons kept putting guns on camera.

King argued that it wasn’t illegal to have a gun. T.I. told him the way they were portraying themselves made it look like something else. He asked the two to imagine the police coming onto the set and asking who owned the guns. “Who raise their hand? Somebody got to raise their hand,” T.I. told them.

Boosie had a warning of his own for King and Tootie: “When y’all got drugs around those legal guns, it’s not legal!” T.I. told them a gun tied to a crime could bring a felony charge. Then he asked why they were so set on making videos with guns when they could write songs about falling in love.

King later said he was putting on a show and described the guns as props. He also had an idea for what he and Tootie could do next: He asked the Zeus Network to give them a reality show.

item.title: Jay-Z’s Super Bowl Halftime Show Is Coming To IMAX Theaters
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jay-Z's first Super Bowl halftime show will screen live at hundreds of IMAX theaters, along with ESPN's game broadcast.
item.content:encoded:
Jay-Z‘s first Super Bowl halftime show is coming to movie theaters. IMAX will screen Super Bowl LXI live at hundreds of locations in the United States and select international markets, Variety reported.

The February 14, 2027, screening will carry ESPN’s main broadcast from SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The presentation includes the game, Jay-Z’s Apple Music halftime show and ESPN’s pregame and postgame coverage.

It will be the first Super Bowl in IMAX theaters and the company’s largest live event to date. IMAX is working with Disney, ESPN and the NFL on the screenings, following live sports programming that included Formula One.

“Watching the Super Bowl with your fellow fans is one of the great shared experiences in sports,” Ken Potrock, Disney’s president of major event integration, said in a statement. IMAX expects theater tickets to go on sale in January and hasn’t announced the participating locations.

The theater screenings give fans another way to watch a game that already has several outlets. ESPN will produce the Super Bowl for the first time, and the broadcast will air on ESPN and ABC and stream live on Disney+. The NFL also lists mobile viewing through NFL+.

For Jay-Z, it’s a return to SoFi.

He closed his anniversary run there in October, bringing Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too $hort out for the final night. The run marked 30 years since Reasonable Doubt.

Jay-Z’s Roc Nation has worked with the NFL on halftime shows since 2019, but this will be the rapper’s first time performing on the Super Bowl stage. “From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” he said in the NFL’s original announcement.

Roc Nation will executive produce the halftime telecast, with Hamish Hamilton directing. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said that when the league first made its deal with Roc Nation, he asked Jay-Z to perform when the timing felt right.

The first push for those theater screenings starts before the end of football season. IMAX will begin running promotional spots during Thanksgiving week.

item.title: Donald Trump Posts Doctored Image Of Nvidia CEO Holding A Red Bra
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Donald Trump posted an altered photo showing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raising a red bra after the board restored him to the job.
item.content:encoded:
Donald Trump marked Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO by posting a doctored picture of the chip executive holding up a red bra. The image, shared on November 23, copied a photograph taken after the 2024 assassination attempt against Trump at a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania.

In Trump’s Truth Social post, Huang takes Trump’s place and appears bloodied, surrounded by figures in suits. He raises the bra where Trump raised his fist in the original photograph. The American flag in the background has been replaced by one bearing the Nvidia logo.

The post came as Nvidia announced that Huang had returned as president, chief executive and a director. The company’s filing says the board acted on November 22; Nvidia made the decision public the following day. Its board said the vote was unanimous.

The board accepted Huang’s resignation on November 11; Nvidia announced his departure the next day. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress took over as interim CEO, and the board initially told investors it did not plan to bring him back.

Trump said in an interview with CNBC that he spoke to directors and helped secure Huang’s return. Discussing the attention over Huang’s conduct, Trump said, “Sex sells, fellas,” and suggested the episode could ultimately be a “net positive” for him.

CNBC’s Sara Eisen pressed him on why the president was getting involved in who runs a public company. Trump said he was acting for the country. Nvidia separately said senior U.S. officials provided input and the board was satisfied that Huang’s return posed no national security risk.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said in the company’s announcement. He thanked Kress and other executives for leading Nvidia during his absence.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer took issue with the reinstatement and told Axios that Democrats intended to investigate. His criticism was directed at the decision and Trump’s involvement, rather than at the altered picture itself.

When Huang stepped down, 50 Cent had already joked about giving him a job on his own AI venture.

Nvidia says its independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort will continue.

item.title: Russ Cuts Houston Listening Party Short After Fans Talk Over His Music
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Russ says Houston was the only one of 16 free listening parties he cut short after people talked over his unreleased songs.
item.content:encoded:
Russ ended a free Houston listening party early after people kept talking over his unreleased music.

The Atlanta rapper said it was the only one of 16 listening events he had to cut short.

The event at downtown vinyl bar Off The Record was billed as a first-come, first-served preview of The Elephant & The Rider. According to the venue’s listing, fans could get in for free and hear the project with Russ in the room.

Videos from the event showed Russ asking people to quiet down and security escorting fans out. One attendee said she was in the second group admitted and found the room emptying when she returned from the restroom.

The rapper told the room he welcomed talk about the songs they had just heard. In footage reviewed by Chron, he drew a line at unrelated conversations while the music was playing.

Russ explained in a TikTok post that he personally books and pays for the free parties. He said he wanted to hear how fans reacted in the room, but that people kept chatting over the tracks even after he told them what the night meant to him. Security had to step in repeatedly, according to his account.

“I don’t tolerate disrespect from my own family lol and I’m certainly not gonna pay money out of my pocket to be disrespected,” he wrote.

The format came out of a New York vinyl bar event for his previous album. “We did a vinyl bar listening party in New York, and I was like, wow, what if we just do this everywhere?” Russ told The Cold Magazine when the series reached London.

In London, Russ played “Recognize,” his collaboration with singer Jessy Blakemore, who joined him in the room. When he asked the crowd to sing along, he realized the hook never came back at the end. He told the magazine that hearing the song with fans in the room made him want to bring the hook back.

Russ has spoken to AllHipHop about staying independent and keeping control of when his music comes out. In Houston, he said the experience would factor into whether he hosted another listening party in the city.

item.title: Yella Beezy Reportedly Files Notice Of Appeal In MO3 Murder Case
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Yella Beezy's lawyer reportedly files notice to challenge the Dallas murder conviction that put him in prison for life.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy‘s lawyer has reportedly filed a notice of appeal in the MO3 murder case. Dallas court reporter Bryson “Boom” Paul said attorney Michael Mowla filed the notice with the Dallas County clerk on November 20, nine days after a jury convicted the rapper of capital murder.

The reported filing follows trial attorney Toby Shook’s announcement that the defense would challenge the verdict.

The notice is the first step in asking a higher court to review the conviction. The report did not identify the arguments Mowla plans to make.

The November 11 verdict came six years to the day after MO3 was killed on Interstate 35E in Dallas. Judge Chika Anyiam sentenced Yella Beezy to life without parole after jurors found him guilty of hiring Kewon White to carry out the shooting.

A bystander was also shot and survived, according to the Dallas County District Attorney’s Office.

“Today, on the anniversary of his death, we hope this verdict brings them some measure of peace,” Dallas County District Attorney John Creuzot said after the conviction, referring to MO3’s family.

The trial came down in part to what prosecutors said was a $40,000 payment. The defense argued that the state had not proved that money withdrawn after MO3’s death paid for the killing.

“This is capital murder, and the state has brought you a lot of speculation,” defense attorney John Gussio said in closing arguments..

White was convicted separately in September and is also serving life without parole. White filed his own notice of appeal in September. A third defendant, Devin Brown, pleaded guilty to murder on November 19 and received a 10-year sentence.

The reported filing does not change the sentence. Yella Beezy is serving his sentence at the W.F. Ramsey Unit in Rosharon, Texas.

Under Texas appellate rules, the trial court clerk forwards a criminal notice of appeal to the appeals court and the court reporter responsible for preparing the record.

If the case proceeds to briefing, the judges will review the trial record for the legal errors the defense identifies rather than retrial before another jury.

item.title: 2 Chainz Shares Footage Of Damaged Vehicle After Apparent Crash
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: 2 Chainz shared a video of a damaged vehicle off a road. The footage does not establish who was in it or where it happened.
item.content:encoded:
2 Chainz shared video of a damaged vehicle off a road in an Instagram Story posted Monday, November 23.

The footage shows his orange-and-black Cybertruck on grass beside the road in the dark, with damage near the front wheel and light-colored debris nearby.

The clip does not show an impact or identify the location. It is unclear who was in the vehicle or whether anyone was injured.

The rapper previously shared footage from a separate crash in Miami on December 9, 2023. Florida Highway Patrol told WSVN that three vehicles were involved on State Road 112 near Northwest 22nd Avenue. AllHipHop reported at the time that the rapper posted a video from an ambulance.

Only one person was taken to a hospital. WSVN identified him as 2 Chainz and reported that he was in South Florida for Art Basel.

In a follow-up after that 2023 crash, 2 Chainz thanked people who had checked on him after he left the hospital. He wrote, “I truly felt the love and don’t worry bout me, I’m good, shake back king.”

In his December 2023 update, the rapper shared an image of what he said was the car that struck the one he was in from behind. He also told followers, “Things could have been worse, but it wasn’t.”

The new Story appeared as 2 Chainz prepares to release Playaz Only Live Once with producer Statik Selektah. He calls it his 10th studio album in an Instagram post. His official store lists December 4 as the release date, and Apple Music lists 18 tracks under his Million Dollar Habits label and EMPIRE.

The pair have already released “Situation,” which features Big Sean, Erykah Badu and Aasher Saintt. The record follows “A Week In Paris,” another preview of the project. Cash Cobain and Young Nudy joined 2 Chainz on the earlier single “Reign.”

He is also listed to join Lil Wayne on two of Wayne’s Carter anniversary shows in December. The first is scheduled for the album’s release day at Rupp Arena in Lexington, Kentucky. They are listed again the following night at Enmarket Arena in Savannah, Georgia.

item.title: Pete Rock & AMXXR Break Down “DopeBoySoul,” AI In Hip-Hop & The Power Of Patience
item.dc:creator: Chuck Creekmur (@ChuckCreekmur)
item.description: Pete Rock and Tru Soul signee AMXXR tell Chuck “Jigsaw” Creekmur how 12 beats "DopeBoySoul" and the opportunity of a lifetime.
item.content:encoded:
Pete Rock Gave AMXXR 12 Beats. It Took Years for Them to Make DopeBoySoul

Rising sensation AMXXR says Pete Rock gave him 12 beats around 2014 or 2015. He didn’t realize the producer had handed him the makings of an album. By then, he’d already spent years watching Pete work, going back to the producer’s days with the late, great Heavy D. Pete remembers him as a student soaking up everything around him. Then he heard AMXXR rap.

Pete has been building records around distinctive voices for decades. On 1992’s Mecca and the Soul Brother, his saxophone loop gave C.L. Smooth room to tell a family story on “They Reminisce Over You (T.R.O.Y.).” More than 30 years later, Pete and Common earned a Best Rap Album Grammy nomination for The Auditorium, Vol. 1.

Now AMXXR, a Mount Vernon rapper and the first artist signed to Pete’s Tru Soul Records, gets a full album of his own with the producer. DopeBoySoul is due December 4 and led by “What You Gonna Do.” At WonWorld Studios, the two recalled the missed opportunity, the call that settled AMXXR’s nerves and the studio lesson that taught him to let a beat breathe. The conversation got just as candid when it turned to AI, ownership and what Pete wishes he’d learned in the ’90s.

Edited for length and clarity. Some questions were condensed. Watch the video for extended conversation.

AllHipHop: What brought y’all together?

Pete Rock: From the days I was doing all that stuff, he was right there watching me on the side. He was younger, much younger. I had some success with Heavy D, and it just grew from there. He was a student, just soaking it up like a sponge. And then one day I heard him rap and was like, “Yo, what’s up?”

AMXXR: That was 2014, 2015. He gave me 12 beats, and I missed the boat because I didn’t know his process. One beat sounded fully complete, but I didn’t know he technically gave me an album then to work on. As the universe may have it, or God’s will, a couple years later he circled back. We got to it with bringing me over to Tru Soul, and we just took it from there.

AllHipHop: How did “What You Gonna Do” become the first single?

AMXXR: He sent it over. He said, “Yo, this is the hit. I’m telling you. Listen to how this sound.” I know his excitement when he texted it to me after him and Jamie had mixed it. I saw exclamation points. I was in the car, I played it. I said, “Oh, now he ain’t lying. This joint smacking.” And then when they put the sauce on it with the mastering, it came through a lot heavier. That’s when I understood the difference between Pete Rock and P Rock the Great.

AllHipHop: Pete, you’re coming off the Common project and all those accolades. What made you want to do a whole album with a newer artist?

Pete Rock: It’s about really creating celebrities with the work I do. You know what I’m saying? It’s my job as a musician. And I think what we’re doing is very special. I produced the album, but I wanted him to get the most shine. I’m not the type of producer to get in anyone’s way, especially when I feel positive about what we’re doing. So I’m very happy for him.

AllHipHop: What’s it like being produced by Pete Rock?

AMXXR: Dream come true, first and foremost. But as an artist, it’s natural to get intimidated. I wasn’t scared. I think there’s a healthy level of intimidation, like when you get drafted to the NBA and Phil Jackson’s your coach, and you know what his expectations are of you as a player.

For 72 hours I had to sit with this. I remember calling him. He said, “Yo, man, just rap. I got you.” And when he said it to me, it was that simple. It just settled in. And then I got to knocking out the records.

AllHipHop: What do y’all think about the state of Hip-Hop now?

Pete Rock: I feel like the originality is coming back, with me being here, a couple other producers that are doing some good things out there. And I feel like the more we do it, the more it lands back in our lap. Even the youth that’s out there doing music can learn how to create and care more about it. Care more about the culture, man.

Lyrics are important. Talk about something that’s really happening. Talk about a little bit of reality. You ain’t got to do your whole album like that, but let me know you tapped in, because there’s a lot going on out here.

AllHipHop: What about when somebody asks AI to make a Pete Rock beat?

AMXXR: There’s an ethical dilemma with AI. There’s an ethical and non-ethical usage of the tool, right? If these companies can keep people on this application and sell ad space or get people to pay for the subscription, their bottom line is follow the money. I totally agree with what he says. It can’t recreate that soul. But if a company don’t want the soul, they want to just make a quick dollar and then cash out like they did with NFTs, it’s the same cycle.

The conversation turned to who holds power in Hip-Hop and what the industry could have done differently.

Pete Rock: There’s certain things I wish I would have learned as a younger man to help combat some of this stuff that we’re going through. And so I take it as, I feel like this is my fault. My fault and people that don’t realize that it was their fault, too. We had an opportunity. The whole ’90s was an opportunity, actually.

AllHipHop: AMXXR, what are people going to hear from you on DopeBoySoul?

AMXXR: It’s in the middle. It’s not too preachy. It’s the core of who I am and things that I’ve seen over these elaborate soundscapes that you can’t really lose on if you know what to do. The first two years under Tru Soul, I had to learn how to approach the production. A few times I was jumping on the records early. He said, “Yo, you got to let it breathe, man.”

Pete Rock: Just lay back. Lay on it, you know what I’m saying? And practice it. And when you hear me say, “That’s it,” you keep practicing that same thing so I don’t have to say nothing else to you.

AMXXR: And that’s what happened. When you getting that from somebody with that level of success and experience, and they willing to share, you got to take heed and move forward. For me, this is a summation of all those experiences, all those teachings, all those life stories that happened prior, put into the product.

item.title: Idris Elba Traces His First Break To A Grant Worth About $1,960 In New Netflix Film
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Idris Elba's Netflix documentary starts with the grant that got him into theater and follows three young people finding their way.
item.content:encoded:
Idris Elba got a grant from The Prince’s Trust as a teenager worth about $1,960 in U.S. dollars at November 2026 exchange rates. It helped him get into the National Youth Music Theatre, a step the actor and DJ looks back on in The Trust. Netflix’s new trailer arrived Monday, November 23,, with the film set for December 26.

The film pairs Elba with King Charles III, who founded the charity in 1976 when he was the Prince of Wales. It also follows three young people getting support through the organization now. The project comes from 22 Summers, the production company Elba started with Diene Petterle and Gina Carter.

Elba grew up in Hackney and knew what it was like to want training his family couldn’t pay for. “They gave me £1,500, because my parents didn’t have enough money,” he said in a speech to Parliament about who gets the chance to work in British television. Elba had worked fitting tires in Dagenham and spent nights on a Ford factory shift before making a living as an actor.

In this archival Sky News report, Elba and the King discuss youth violence at an earlier Trust event.

Acting wasn’t the only way Elba made a living. “A large part of my career when I was acting, I was eating by DJing,” he told AllHipHop in an interview about playing Stringer Bell on The Wire. He came up through pirate radio and the sound system circuit in London, where reggae and dancehall drew him in before Hip-Hop.

Elba and his wife, Sabrina, started the Elba Hope Foundation, which teamed up with the now-renamed King’s Trust on Creative Futures. The program started in 2024 and has offered training in DJing, theater and visual arts.

Britain’s Department for Culture, Media and Sport announced about $652,000 in funding (£500,000) in 2025 to expand the program to 400 more people aged 16 to 30 across England. The department said more than 100 young people had already taken part during the first year.

Creative Futures and WME NXT launched a free, six-week online program on October 12. It uses Elba’s career to show young people what producers, agents and managers do, alongside paths into music, film and television. Participants don’t need any industry experience.

Ashley Francis-Roy directs The Trust, with Clare Bradbury serving as showrunner.

item.title: Shyne Plans 2027 Memoir As He Gets Back To Music
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Shyne lays out plans for a 2027 memoir and an album with Dr. Dre, Swizz Beatz and more ahead of Rock the Bells in Newark.
item.content:encoded:
Shyne plans to publish The Book of Moses in 2027, turning his spiritual evolution into a memoir as he gets back onstage. The rapper also named eight producers working on his upcoming album, The Honorable.

In an interview with Black Enterprise, Shyne said the book will trace his path from Orthodox Judaism to a broader spiritual outlook focused on compassion and integrity. He named Dr. Dre, Swizz Beatz, Timbaland, RZA, Hit-Boy, Boi-1da, The Heatmakerz and Polow da Don among the album’s producers.

Shyne had already talked about making The Honorable after Hulu released its documentary on him in 2024. In an earlier interview on Cam’ron’s Talk With Flee, as Black Enterprise reported, he compared the idea to Jay-Z’s American Gangster: a record inspired by a film that stands on its own rather than a soundtrack.

Before the memoir, Shyne has a show in Newark. He said LL Cool J invited him to Rock the Bells himself. “When Uncle L reaches out, and they say, ‘Shyne, we want you on the stage,’ you don’t say no.”

Ahead of that Brooklyn homecoming, Shyne told BET what it meant to headline in the neighborhood where he grew up.

Prudential Center lists Shyne on the Sunday, November 29 bill alongside LL Cool J, Lil’ Kim and Method Man & Redman. Raekwon, Ghostface Killah and SWV are also scheduled to perform at the show, which starts at 7 p.m.

Newark follows Shyne’s sold-out May 2 homecoming at Brooklyn’s Kings Theatre, where he revisited his self-titled debut album. Garifuna drummers opened the night, and Juelz Santana, Lil’ Cease and AZ joined him onstage. Shyne closed the show with “Bad Boyz,” as AllHipHop reported from the concert.

His debut landed at No. 5 on the Billboard 200 in 2000. It paired him with dancehall singer Barrington Levy on “Bad Boyz” and “Bonnie & Shyne.”

Outside of music, Shyne told Black Enterprise that he plans to seek a return to Belize’s Parliament in 2030. He represented Mesopotamia and served as the House of Representatives’ opposition leader before losing his seat in 2025. He also plans to open a Belize outpost of Brooklyn Chop House in 2027.

item.title: Michael Hampton, Parliament-Funkadelic Guitarist Who Shaped Hip-Hop, Dies At 70
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Michael Hampton, the Parliament-Funkadelic guitarist whose playing reached rap records by Dr. Dre and Ice Cube, has died at 70.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Hampton, the Parliament-Funkadelic guitarist whose playing reached Hip-Hop records by Dr. Dre, Ice Cube and Digital Underground, has died at 70.

Los Angeles venue Zebulon, where he recently performed, announced his death on Instagram, Stereogum reported on November 23. No cause of death was reported.

Fans knew the Cleveland guitarist as Kidd Funkadelic, a nickname he earned after joining George Clinton’s band at 17.

Clinton’s official biography of Hampton traces the hire to an afterparty where the teenager played Eddie Hazel’s ten-minute “Maggot Brain” solo note for note.

Hazel played the original “Maggot Brain.” Hampton made the piece his own onstage, improvising more over the years.

A live version with Hampton appeared on the bonus EP that came with Funkadelic’s 1978 album One Nation Under a Groove.

Hampton made his Funkadelic recording debut on 1975’s Let’s Take It to the Stage. Later records gave rap producers another way into his work.

KMUW’s interview with Hampton traces his guitar from Parliament’s “Mothership Connection (Star Child)” to Dr. Dre’s “Let Me Ride” and from Funkadelic’s “One Nation Under a Groove” to Ice Cube’s “Bop Gun.” Digital Underground’s “Kiss You Back” drew on “(Not Just) Knee Deep.”

Hampton’s work with Digital Underground went beyond sampling. His artist biography lists him as a co-writer on “Wussup Wit the Luv” and credits him on two Too $hort albums. He also toured with Deee-Lite alongside Bootsy Collins.

Recording sessions for Funkadelic and Bootsy’s Rubber Band often overlapped. Hampton told Guitar World that musicians recorded around the clock and much of the work went undocumented.

“You play the songs, rehearse them and do the shows, but you don’t know it’s gonna be something that loops on forever,” he said.

The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inducted Hampton with Parliament-Funkadelic in 1997, with Prince presenting the honor.

He put out his first solo album, Heavy Metal Funkason, in 1998 and later released King Kong, an instrumental project built around the story of the giant ape.

Clinton’s catalog kept turning up in rap. Hampton was still touring with Parliament-Funkadelic this year and had recently played his own show in Los Angeles.
